      "stdout": "===== 7nm/run.tcl =====
# =============================================================================
# AutoCell 7nm FinFET (tcbn7) TCL Example
#
# A small, self-contained standard-cell example that drives the *complete*
# AutoCell TCL flow - technology setup, netlist load, place & route, LVS - for a
# handful of gates from an N7-class standard-cell library.
#
# It is the 7nm FinFET counterpart of the `dram` example: the same run.tcl
# entry point and the same seven split technology files (layers.tcl,
# layer_functions.tcl, viadefs.tcl, globals.tcl, rules.tcl, place.tcl,
# route.tcl) sourced in dependency order, plus a cells/ tree of per-cell
# netlists and placements - but built on a real (N7-class) FinFET
# technology instead of a hand-written planar one.  The front-end foundry
# deck is carried verbatim into the split files, and the cell schematics come
# from the cells/ tree.  See README.md for the full background and a tour of
# the flow.
#
# =============================================================================

# Database
option gds_dbu 0.0005
option design_grid 0.0005
option tech_unit 0.0001

option compaction 0
option lvs_case_sensitive 1
option lvs_join_symmetric_nets 0

option finfet_metal_coloring 0
option finfet_central_gate_interconnection 1
option finfet_isolate_gate_interconnection 1
option finfet_optimize_via_spacing 1
option finfet_convert_power_contacts 1
option finfet_insert_filler_active 1

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 0 - locate this example and the shipped 7nm technology
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# $tcl_script_path is this run.tcl, so case_dir is the 7nm example folder.
#
# The technology is self-contained in this directory: the full 7nm FinFET
# front-end foundry deck (CAD layers, layer functions, via definitions, global
# power/ground/body nets and design rules) plus the placement / routing objects
# (* PG connectors, cell boundary, device classes, placer templates,
# signal-pin template and routing grids) are split across the seven focused
# files sourced below in dependency order - the same split the `dram` example
# uses.  Each file carries its section of the shipped deck
# (test/test_case/tcbn7/library/tech.tcl) / layout_spec verbatim, so the example
# is self-contained and does not modify the original deck.
set case_dir  [file dirname [file nativename $tcl_script_path]]
set tech_home "${case_dir}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source the seven split technology files (dependency order)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   layers.tcl            - CAD layers + their roles (tech add_layer -functions)
#   layer_functions.tcl   - documentation of the layer roles (see layers.tcl)
#   viadefs.tcl           - via / contact stack definitions (add_viadef) + mapping
#   globals.tcl           - global power / ground / body net naming (set_global_net)
#   rules.tcl             - design rules (add_rule) + multi-patterning layer coloring
#   place.tcl             - PG connectors, boundary, device classes, placer templates
#   route.tcl             - router options, signal-pin template, routing grids
source [file join $case_dir "layers.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "layer_functions.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "viadefs.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "globals.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "rules.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "place.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "route.tcl"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 1 - flow options
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
option legalizer              2

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 2 - declare which cells to build
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three simple combinational gates, mirroring the
# `dram` example's inverter + 2-input-gate selection:
#
#   INVD1H240L11P57  - inverter  (1 row)  - 1 NMOS + 1 PMOS
#   ND2D1H240L11P57  - 2-input NAND (1 row) - 2 NMOS (series) + 2 PMOS (parallel)
#   NR2D1H240L11P57  - 2-input NOR  (1 row) - 2 NMOS (parallel) + 2 PMOS (series)
#
# The NAND puts the NMOS pull-down in series; the NOR puts the PMOS pull-up in
# series - the two complementary transistor-network topologies of CMOS logic.
#
# To build more cells, add them to $example_cells and give their row count in
# $cell_row_map below.
set example_cells [list \
    INVD1H240L11P57 \
    ND2D1H240L11P57 \
    NR2D1H240L11P57 \
]

# Row count per cell = how many standard-cell rows the cell occupies.  All
# three gates above are single-row (1) cells.
set cell_row_map [dict create \
    INVD1H240L11P57 1 \
    ND2D1H240L11P57 1 \
    NR2D1H240L11P57 1 \
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 3 - load the cell netlists
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# read_netlist imports the flattened transistor netlist for the requested cells
# and classifies every device as PMOS / NMOS against the device classes that the
# technology defines (pch_lvt_mac / nch_lvt_mac).  Each .SUBCKT
# becomes a named schematic that the `cell` command references below.
#
# The same per-cell netlist is also kept (for reading) under
#   cells/<cell>/schematic/sch.cdl
# so the directory layout matches the `dram` example.
read_netlist -cells $example_cells \
    -pmos_set {pch_lvt_mac} \
    -nmos_set {nch_lvt_mac} \
    -file "${tech_home}/7nm_stdcells.spi"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 4 - build each cell (place + route + LVS)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
foreach cell_name $example_cells {

    # number of standard-cell rows for this cell
    set row [dict get $cell_row_map $cell_name]
    option placer_row_count $row

    # --- create the cell ---------------------------------------------------
    # Bind the cell to the 7nm technology, its netlist (schematic), and the
    # library's shared boundary / dummy templates.  These * objects are
    # defined by the sourced technology (see place.tcl / route.tcl).
    cell $cell_name -tech default_tech -schematic $cell_name \
        -boundary boundary \
        -dummy   dummy_template

    # --- device folding ----------------------------------------------------
    # 7nm devices are fin-based and sized in fins (nfin).  Auto-folding splits a
    # wide device into parallel fingers so it fits the row height.
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class pch_lvt_mac -range {0.038 0.098} -width 0.038
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class nch_lvt_mac -range {0.038 0.098} -width 0.038

    # --- (optional) replay a saved placement -------------------------------
    # Leave commented to let AutoCell place the devices automatically.
    # Uncomment to replay the saved placement kept under cells/<cell>/layout/.
    cell $cell_name read_placement \
         -file "${case_dir}/cells/${cell_name}/layout/placement.json" \
         -type json -top_cell $cell_name

    # --- configure the router ----------------------------------------------
    # Map technology layers to routing grids (PO->poly, MP->m1g, MD->m1,
    # M1->m2, M2->m3) and select the signal-pin template.
    cell $cell_name set_router \
        -grid_map [dict create \
            PO poly \
            MP m1g \
            MD m1 \
            M1 m2 \
            M2 m3] \
        -pin_template pin

    # --- generate the layout -----------------------------------------------
    # Places the devices, runs the router, and performs an internal LVS check
    # (layout vs. schematic) for the cell.
    cell $cell_name generate_layout
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 5 - export the result
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Write all generated cells to a single GDS file - the industry format handed to
# the fab for manufacturing.
set FileName "7nm_example.gds"
write_layout -cells $example_cells -type gds -file $FileName

puts "======================================================================"
puts " 7nm (tcbn7) example finished successfully."
puts "   GDS output   : $FileName"
puts "   Cells        : [join $example_cells {, }]"
puts "======================================================================"

{
  "path": "/proj/train/AI/workdir/e0031982/eda_sandbox_flow/sessions/default_cline-eval-001_EDA-Eval-DesignFlow-AutoCellTclFlow-001_0/ref/7nm/run.tcl",
  "content": "# =============================================================================
# AutoCell 7nm FinFET (tcbn7) TCL Example
#
# A small, self-contained standard-cell example that drives the *complete*
# AutoCell TCL flow - technology setup, netlist load, place & route, LVS - for a
# handful of gates from an N7-class standard-cell library.
#
# It is the 7nm FinFET counterpart of the `dram` example: the same run.tcl
# entry point and the same seven split technology files (layers.tcl,
# layer_functions.tcl, viadefs.tcl, globals.tcl, rules.tcl, place.tcl,
# route.tcl) sourced in dependency order, plus a cells/ tree of per-cell
# netlists and placements - but built on a real (N7-class) FinFET
# technology instead of a hand-written planar one.  The front-end foundry
# deck is carried verbatim into the split files, and the cell schematics come
# from the cells/ tree.  See README.md for the full background and a tour of
# the flow.
#
# =============================================================================

# Database
option gds_dbu 0.0005
option design_grid 0.0005
option tech_unit 0.0001

option compaction 0
option lvs_case_sensitive 1
option lvs_join_symmetric_nets 0

option finfet_metal_coloring 0
option finfet_central_gate_interconnection 1
option finfet_isolate_gate_interconnection 1
option finfet_optimize_via_spacing 1
option finfet_convert_power_contacts 1
option finfet_insert_filler_active 1

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 0 - locate this example and the shipped 7nm technology
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# $tcl_script_path is this run.tcl, so case_dir is the 7nm example folder.
#
# The technology is self-contained in this directory: the full 7nm FinFET
# front-end foundry deck (CAD layers, layer functions, via definitions, global
# power/ground/body nets and design rules) plus the placement / routing objects
# (* PG connectors, cell boundary, device classes, placer templates,
# signal-pin template and routing grids) are split across the seven focused
# files sourced below in dependency order - the same split the `dram` example
# uses.  Each file carries its section of the shipped deck
# (test/test_case/tcbn7/library/tech.tcl) / layout_spec verbatim, so the example
# is self-contained and does not modify the original deck.
set case_dir  [file dirname [file nativename $tcl_script_path]]
set tech_home "${case_dir}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source the seven split technology files (dependency order)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   layers.tcl            - CAD layers + their roles (tech add_layer -functions)
#   layer_functions.tcl   - documentation of the layer roles (see layers.tcl)
#   viadefs.tcl           - via / contact stack definitions (add_viadef) + mapping
#   globals.tcl           - global power / ground / body net naming (set_global_net)
#   rules.tcl             - design rules (add_rule) + multi-patterning layer coloring
#   place.tcl             - PG connectors, boundary, device classes, placer templates
#   route.tcl             - router options, signal-pin template, routing grids
source [file join $case_dir "layers.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "layer_functions.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "viadefs.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "globals.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "rules.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "place.tcl"]
source [file join $case_dir "route.tcl"]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 1 - flow options
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
option legalizer              2

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 2 - declare which cells to build
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Three simple combinational gates, mirroring the
# `dram` example's inverter + 2-input-gate selection:
#
#   INVD1H240L11P57  - inverter  (1 row)  - 1 NMOS + 1 PMOS
#   ND2D1H240L11P57  - 2-input NAND (1 row) - 2 NMOS (series) + 2 PMOS (parallel)
#   NR2D1H240L11P57  - 2-input NOR  (1 row) - 2 NMOS (parallel) + 2 PMOS (series)
#
# The NAND puts the NMOS pull-down in series; the NOR puts the PMOS pull-up in
# series - the two complementary transistor-network topologies of CMOS logic.
#
# To build more cells, add them to $example_cells and give their row count in
# $cell_row_map below.
set example_cells [list \
    INVD1H240L11P57 \
    ND2D1H240L11P57 \
    NR2D1H240L11P57 \
]

# Row count per cell = how many standard-cell rows the cell occupies.  All
# three gates above are single-row (1) cells.
set cell_row_map [dict create \
    INVD1H240L11P57 1 \
    ND2D1H240L11P57 1 \
    NR2D1H240L11P57 1 \
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 3 - load the cell netlists
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# read_netlist imports the flattened transistor netlist for the requested cells
# and classifies every device as PMOS / NMOS against the device classes that the
# technology defines (pch_lvt_mac / nch_lvt_mac).  Each .SUBCKT
# becomes a named schematic that the `cell` command references below.
#
# The same per-cell netlist is also kept (for reading) under
#   cells/<cell>/schematic/sch.cdl
# so the directory layout matches the `dram` example.
read_netlist -cells $example_cells \
    -pmos_set {pch_lvt_mac} \
    -nmos_set {nch_lvt_mac} \
    -file "${tech_home}/7nm_stdcells.spi"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHASE 4 - build each cell (place + route + LVS)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
foreach cell_name $example_cells {

    # number of standard-cell rows for this cell
    set row [dict get $cell_row_map $cell_name]
    option placer_row_count $row

    # --- create the cell ---------------------------------------------------
    # Bind the cell to the 7nm technology, its netlist (schematic), and the
    # library's shared boundary / dummy templates.  These * objects are
    # defined by the sourced technology (see place.tcl / route.tcl).
    cell $cell_name -tech default_tech -schematic $cell_name \
        -boundary boundary \
        -dummy   dummy_template

    # --- device folding ----------------------------------------------------
    # 7nm devices are fin-based and sized in fins (nfin).  Auto-folding splits a
    # wide device into parallel fingers so it fits the row height.
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class pch_lvt_mac -range {0.038 0.098} -width 0.038

#
# IC context (see doc/knowledge/IC_Design_Glossary_for_Beginners.md):
#   Routing is the "wiring" half of place & route: after the devices/templates
#   are placed, AutoCell draws the metal wires (plus vias and contacts) that
#   connect the transistor terminals into the intended logic.  A routing *grid*
#   is the set of allowed wire tracks on a layer - wires snap to these tracks

{
  "path": "/proj/train/AI/workdir/e0031982/eda_sandbox_flow/sessions/default_cline-eval-001_EDA-Eval-DesignFlow-AutoCellTclFlow-001_0/ref/dram/run.tcl",
  "content": "# =============================================================================
# AutoCell DRAM Example - Main Flow Script (tech + flow merged)
#
# This single script both defines the technology and runs the full layout flow
# for a small DRAM-style standard cell library. It is written to teach the
# end-to-end AutoCell TCL flow:
#
#   PART A  (technology)  process, geometric constants and the split tech files
#   PHASE 1 (setup)       locate files and load the technology
#   PHASE 2 (netlist)     read the transistor netlist of the cells to build
#   PHASE 3 (build)       for each cell: create the cell, place devices,
#                         route wires, and generate the final GDS layout
#
# Cells built by this example (each cell has its own schematic at
# cells/<name>/schematic/sch.cdl):
#   invX1      - 1-input inverter            (2 transistors)
#   nand2X1    - 2-input NAND                (4 transistors)
#   buf2X1     - 2-stage buffer / 2 inverters (4 transistors)
#
# Run it from this directory with the AutoCell binary:
#     autocell run.tcl
# (GUI users can also open examples/dram/run.tcl from the Home page.)
#
# The technology itself is split into the seven focused files sourced below
# (layers.tcl, layer_functions.tcl, viadefs.tcl, globals.tcl, rules.tcl,
# place.tcl, route.tcl); this script brings them together and drives the flow.
#
# --- learning pointers ---
# The flow below is a complete *place & route* run (IC glossary: Layout,
# Standard Cell, Place & Route, DRC, LVS, GDS). Each technology file is
# cross-referenced to doc/knowledge/design-rules-glossary.md (layer stack and
# design rules) and doc/knowledge/IC_Design_Glossary_for_Beginners.md (CMOS,
# transistors and standard-cell concepts). The README.md in this directory is a
# guided walk-through of everything on show here.
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# PART A - TECHNOLOGY
# =============================================================================
# Every script knows the directory it lives in through `$tcl_script_path`.
# We anchor all relative file references to that directory so the example can
# be moved around and still run.
set case_dir  [file dirname [file nativename $tcl_script_path]]
set tech_home ${case_dir}

# options
set_option compaction 0
set_option design_grid 0.005
set_option gds_merge_shapes 0
set_option lvs_case_sensitive 1

# ---- technology basics ------------------------------------------------------
# We are building on a planar (non-FinFET) process. All dimensions are microns.
tech -process planar

# ---- geometric constants used throughout the technology ---------------------
# cpp is the "contact poly pitch": the horizontal grid spacing of poly tracks
# (IC glossary: channel / gate; design-rules glossary: pitch = width + space of
# a repeating pattern). Cell widths in the README table are quoted in cpp units.
set cpp 0.5            ;# contact poly pitch (horizontal grid of poly tracks)
set hcpp [expr $cpp / 2]
set height 12.5           ;# standard cell row height in microns
set hh  [expr $height / 2]
set pmos_coord_y 6.625  ;# y-position of the PMOS active (drawn in the top half)
set nmos_coord_y 3.625  ;# y-position of the NMOS active (drawn in the bottom half)

# ---- source the split technology files (dependency order) -------------------
#   layers.tcl            - CAD layers (tech add_layer)
#   layer_functions.tcl   - layer roles (tech set_layer_function)
#   viadefs.tcl           - via / contact stack definitions (tech add_viadef)
#   globals.tcl           - global power / ground net naming
#   rules.tcl             - design rules (tech add_rule): min width / spacing / area
#   place.tcl             - PG connectors, device classes, placer templates,
#                           dummy template, cell boundary
#   route.tcl             - router options, via mapping, pin template, grids
source [ file join $tech_home "layers.tcl" ]
source [ file join $tech_home "layer_functions.tcl" ]
source [ file join $tech_home "viadefs.tcl" ]
source [ file join $tech_home "globals.tcl" ]
source [ file join $tech_home "rules.tcl" ]
source [ file join $tech_home "place.tcl" ]
source [ file join $tech_home "route.tcl" ]

# =============================================================================
# PHASE 1 - DECLARE THE CELLS
# =============================================================================
# Declare which cells we are going to build.
set simple_cells [ list \
    invX1 \
    nand2X1 \
    buf2X1 \
]

# =============================================================================
# PHASE 2 - BUILD EACH CELL
# =============================================================================
foreach cell_name $simple_cells {

    # --- load this cell's schematic -----------------------------------------
    # Each cell keeps its own transistor netlist (a single .SUBCKT) in
    # cells/<name>/schematic/sch.cdl. The `schematic` command parses that file
    # and binds its transistor models (pch_rvt for PMOS, nch_rvt for NMOS) to
    # the corresponding device classes defined in place.tcl.
    schematic $cell_name \
        -spice_path "${tech_home}/cells/${cell_name}/schematic/sch.cdl" \
        -pmos_classes { pch_rvt } \
        -nmos_classes { nch_rvt }

    # --- create the cell -----------------------------------------------------
    # Instantiate the cell: which technology, which schematic, and which
    # boundary & dummy templates to use for its frame.
    cell $cell_name -tech default_tech \
        -schematic $cell_name \
        -boundary boundary \
        -dummy dummy_template \
        -device_classes { pch_rvt nch_rvt }

    # --- device folding ------------------------------------------------------
    # Controls auto-folding of wide transistors: any transistor whose width
    # falls in the given range (<width> threshold) is folded into parallel
    # fingers so it fits in the row.
    # (Wide devices are split into parallel fingers to raise drive strength
    # while keeping a compact, manufacturable layout.)
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class pch_rvt -range {3.375 4.5} -width 3.75
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class nch_rvt -range {1.875 2.5} -width 1.875

    # --- optional: placement from a JSON file -------------------------------
    # Standard cells are often pre-placed by hand / previous runs. `read_placement`
    # restores such a placement so AutoCell can route the exact same layout.
    # (Remove this call to let AutoCell place the devices automatically.)
    # cell $cell_name read_placement -file_path "${tech_home}/cells/${cell_name}/layout/placement.json" -type json

    # --- choose the placer templates ----------------------------------------
    # Template strips tell the placer where NMOS and PMOS transistors may sit.
    # matched_template carries both an NMOS (low in the row) and a PMOS (high
    # in the row); pmos/nmos templates cover cells with an unbalanced count.
    cell $cell_name set_placer -templates { matched_template pmos_template nmos_template }

    # --- configure the router -----------------------------------------------
    # Map technology layers to routing grids, choose the signal-pin template
    # and the PG (power/ground) connectors.
    cell $cell_name set_router \
        -grid_map [ dict create GATE gate M0 m0 ] \
        -pin_template pin_template \
        -pin_grid pin \
        -vss_connector vss_pgc \
        -vdd_connector vdd_pgc

    # --- generate the layout -------------------------------------------------
    # This is where AutoCell draws the placement, runs the router, and performs
    # an internal LVS check for every cell (LVS = layout vs. schematic - it
    # verifies the drawn geometry actually matches the intended netlist).
    cell $cell_name generate_layout
}

# =============================================================================
# PHASE 3 - WRITE THE RESULT

## Background knowledge

Two companion glossaries in this repository explain the physical-design
vocabulary used on this page. Newcomers are encouraged to skim them once, then
keep them open while reading the example:

- **`doc/knowledge/IC_Design_Glossary_for_Beginners.md`** — CMOS, transistors,
  logic gates, place & route, DRC/LVS, memories (incl. why DRAM needs
  refresh), standard cells, vias and more.
- **`doc/knowledge/design-rules-glossary.md`** — the foundry **design rules**
  and **layer stack** (AA, wells, poly, implants, contacts, metals, vias) that
  every `tech add_rule` below refers to.

Quick facts used throughout the flow:

| Term | Meaning (see glossary for detail) |
|------|-----------------------------------|
| **CMOS** | Complementary MOS: every gate pairs an NMOS and a PMOS so it draws almost no idle power. |
| **NMOS / PMOS** | The two transistor flavors; NMOS pulls output **low**, PMOS pulls output **high**. |
| **Pull-up / pull-down** | In each gate, the PMOS network drives HIGH and the NMOS network drives LOW — exactly one conducts. |
| **Standard cell** | A pre-designed, fixed-height layout block (inverter, NAND, …) snapped together in rows. |
| **Place & route** | EDA steps that place cells and wire them automatically — what this example runs. |
| **Layout** | The geometric blueprint of shapes on every layer, sent to the fab. |
| **DRC / LVS** | Design-rule check + layout-vs-schematic verification (AutoCell runs an internal LVS). |
| **GDS** | The industry file format used to hand the layout to the fab. |
| **Via** | The vertical plug connecting one metal layer to another. |
| **Design rule** | A "layer + relationship + limit" manufacturing constraint, e.g. minimum width/space. |

## The technology in IC terms

The seven technology files encode a simplified planar (non-FinFET) process. The
tables below map the names used in the files onto the standard foundry layer
stack described in `design-rules-glossary.md` — handy for relating AutoCell
`tech` commands to a real process.

### Layers (`layers.tcl`) and their roles (`layer_functions.tcl`)

The front-end layers define where the transistors live:

| AutoCell layer | Foundry role | What it is (glossary) |
|----------------|--------------|-----------------------|
| `AA` | active area (OD) | The silicon islands; the device channel & source/drain sit here. |
| `NW` | N-well | The doped well hosting the PMOS devices. |
| `GATE` | poly (GC) | The polysilicon gate over the channel; also used as a bridge wire. |
| `NPLUS` / `PPLUS` | N+ / P+ source-drain | Heavily doped source/drain implants for NMOS/PMOS. |
| `CT` | contact (CA/CS) | The plug that lands on active or poly. |
| `M0` / `M1` | metal-1 / metal-2 | Wiring layers (here M0 is the main routing + power-rail layer). |
| `VIA1` | via | The vertical connection between M0 and M1. |
| `GATE_DUMMY` | dummy poly | Non-functional filler for density/planarization. |

> **Beginner tip** (from the design-rules glossary): the layer *roles* here use
> terms such as `poly`, `nwell`, `nplus`/`pplus`, `pcont`/`ncont`, `m1`/`m2` and
> `via1`. Those functions drive device recognition, contact landing and
> well/implant polarity during extraction, DRC and LVS — they are the semantic
> glue between a bare GDS layer number and a foundry mask.

### Design rules (`rules.tcl`)

A **design rule** is "layer + geometric relationship + limit". `rules.tcl` uses
three common rule types:

```tcl
tech add_rule -type min_width   -layer "GATE" -value 0.054   ;# min poly width
tech add_rule -type min_spacing -layer { "AA" } -value 0.14   ;# min AA-to-AA space
tech add_rule -type min_area    -layer "M0"   -value 0.01     ;# min metal island area
```

These mirror foundry rule families such as `GC.W.1` (poly width), `AA.S.1`
(active space) or `M1.E.2` (metal enclosure of a contact) in the glossary.

### Vias (`viadefs.tcl`)

A **viadef** stacks two conductive layers through a cut layer, declaring the cut
shape and the required **enclosure** (`layer*_enc`) on each side. Enclosure is
exactly what the foundry glossary calls an "enclosure" rule: how far the metal
must surround the cut so the connection survives misalignment.

From a shell, inside this directory:

## A guided tour of the flow

The whole flow in `run.tcl` is split into three logical phases.

### Phase 1 — Setup
```
source layers, layer_functions, viadefs, globals, place, route  # the technology
option ...             # optional router / placer behaviour switches
```
This is where the process and every layer/rule/via the router and placer will
use are brought into memory.

### Phase 2 — Load each cell's schematic
Inside the per-cell loop the `schematic` command parses that cell's CDL file:
```
schematic $cell_name -spice_path cells/$cell_name/schematic/sch.cdl \
                     -pmos_classes {pch_rvt} -nmos_classes {nch_rvt}
```
Each `pch_rvt`/`nch_rvt` model is bound to the PMOS/NMOS device class defined in
`place.tcl`.

### Phase 3 — Build each cell (inside a TCL `foreach`)
For every cell name the same recipe runs:

```tcl
schematic $cell_name -spice_path ... # load the cell's netlist (sch.cdl)
cell      $cell_name ...              # create the cell (tech, boundary, templates)
cell      $cell_name set_device_folding ...   # auto-fold wide transistors
# cell    $cell_name read_placement ...       # (optional) replay a placement
cell      $cell_name set_placer ...           # choose NMOS/PMOS template strips
cell      $cell_name set_router ...           # map layers->grids, pick pin/PG
cell      $cell_name generate_layout          # place, route, LVS-check, write
```

This is the classic **place & route** pipeline in miniature: place the devices,
choose how to wire them, then run the router and verify.

### Phase 4 — Export
```
write_layout -cells $simple_cells -type gds -file dram_example.gds
```
The result is a **GDS** file — the standard format handed to a fab for
manufacturing (the "layout" milestone in the IC design flow).

# PHASE 2 - BUILD EACH CELL

foreach cell_name $simple_cells {

    # --- load this cell's schematic -----------------------------------------
    # Each cell keeps its own transistor netlist (a single .SUBCKT) in
    # cells/<name>/schematic/sch.cdl. The `schematic` command parses that file
    # and binds its transistor models (pch_rvt for PMOS, nch_rvt for NMOS) to
    # the corresponding device classes defined in place.tcl.
    schematic $cell_name \
        -spice_path "${tech_home}/cells/${cell_name}/schematic/sch.cdl" \
        -pmos_classes { pch_rvt } \
        -nmos_classes { nch_rvt }

    # --- create the cell -----------------------------------------------------
    # Instantiate the cell: which technology, which schematic, and which
    # boundary & dummy templates to use for its frame.
    cell $cell_name -tech default_tech \
        -schematic $cell_name \
        -boundary boundary \
        -dummy dummy_template \
        -device_classes { pch_rvt nch_rvt }

    # --- device folding ------------------------------------------------------
    # Controls auto-folding of wide transistors: any transistor whose width
    # falls in the given range (<width> threshold) is folded into parallel
    # fingers so it fits in the row.
    # (Wide devices are split into parallel fingers to raise drive strength
    # while keeping a compact, manufacturable layout.)
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class pch_rvt -range {3.375 4.5} -width 3.75
    cell $cell_name set_device_folding -class nch_rvt -range {1.875 2.5} -width 1.875

    # --- optional: placement from a JSON file -------------------------------
    # Standard cells are often pre-placed by hand / previous runs. `read_placement`
    # restores such a placement so AutoCell can route the exact same layout.
    # (Remove this call to let AutoCell place the devices automatically.)
    # cell $cell_name read_placement -file_path "${tech_home}/cells/${cell_name}/layout/placement.json" -type json

    # --- choose the placer templates ----------------------------------------
    # Template strips tell the placer where NMOS and PMOS transistors may sit.
    # matched_template carries both an NMOS (low in the row) and a PMOS (high
    # in the row); pmos/nmos templates cover cells with an unbalanced count.
    cell $cell_name set_placer -templates { matched_template pmos_template nmos_template }

    # --- configure the router -----------------------------------------------
    # Map technology layers to routing grids, choose the signal-pin template
    # and the PG (power/ground) connectors.
    cell $cell_name set_router \
        -grid_map [ dict create GATE gate M0 m0 ] \
        -pin_template pin_template \
        -pin_grid pin \
        -vss_connector vss_pgc \
        -vdd_connector vdd_pgc

    # --- generate the layout -------------------------------------------------
    # This is where AutoCell draws the placement, runs the router, and performs
    # an internal LVS check for every cell (LVS = layout vs. schematic - it
    # verifies the drawn geometry actually matches the intended netlist).
    cell $cell_name generate_layout

def render_template(text, ctx):
    def repl(m):
        key = next((m.group(g) for g in ("k","a","l","p","d","h") if m.group(g)), None)
        if key is None: return m.group(0)
        return str(ctx.get(key, m.group(0)))
    return PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(repl, text)

def has_placeholders(text):
    return PLACEHOLDER_RE.search(text) is not None

def has_residue(text):
    return RESIDUE_RE.search(text) is not None

def gen_route(spec):
    r = spec["routing"]
    lines = [_header("route.tcl - via instances, signal-pin template, routing grids")]

    # Via instances (references to the viadefs declared in viadefs.tcl).
    for v in spec["via_definitions"]:
        lines.append("via %s -viadef %s -tech default_tech"
                     % (_q(v["name"]), _q(v["name"])))

    # Signal-pin template (referenced by run.tcl as -pin_template).
    lines.append("pin %s -layer %s" % (r["pin_template"], _q(r["pin_layer"])))

    # Routing grids: every value in grid_map plus the pin grid must be defined.
    grid_objs = {}
    for g in r["grids"]:
        if isinstance(g, dict):
            grid_objs[str(_pick(g, "name", default="grid"))] = g
        elif isinstance(g, str):
            grid_objs[g] = {}
    ordered = []
    for n in list(r["grid_map"].values()) + [r["pin_grid"]]:
        if n and n not in ordered:
            ordered.append(n)
    for n in ordered:
        g = grid_objs.get(n, {})
        cost = _pick(g, "cost", default=None)
        suffix = " -cost %s" % _num(cost) if cost is not None else ""
        lines.append("grid %s%s" % (n, suffix))
    return "\n".join(lines)


def gen_run(spec):
    n = spec["netlist"]
    r = spec["routing"]
    pl = spec["placement"]
    lines = [_header("run.tcl - top-level flow entry")]

    lines.append("")

    lines.append("    cell $cell_name -tech default_tech \\")

        lines.append("    cell $cell_name read_placement \\")

    # Router contract: grid_map, pin_template, pin_grid, vdd/vss connectors.

    lines.append("    cell $cell_name set_router \\")
    lines.append("        -grid_map [dict create %s] \\" % gm)
    lines.append("        -pin_template %s \\" % r["pin_template"])
    lines.append("        -pin_grid %s \\" % r["pin_grid"])
    lines.append("        -vss_connector %s \\" % r["vss_connector"])
    lines.append("        -vdd_connector %s" % r["vdd_connector"])
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("    cell $cell_name generate_layout")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")

    gds = spec["output"]["gds_path"]
    if gds.startswith("$") or gds.startswith("[") or gds.startswith("/"):
        file_expr = gds
    else:

    lines.append("set FileName %s" % file_expr)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Skeleton template rendering (optional baseline with placeholders)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_context(spec):
    ctx = {
        "process": spec["process"],
        "design_name": spec["design_name"],
        "pin_template": spec["routing"]["pin_template"],
        "pin_layer": spec["routing"]["pin_layer"],
        "pin_grid": spec["routing"]["pin_grid"],
        "vdd_connector": spec["routing"]["vdd_connector"],
        "vss_connector": spec["routing"]["vss_connector"],
        "boundary": _boundary_name(spec),
        "dummy_template": _dummy_name(spec),
        "netlist_mode": spec["netlist"]["mode"],
        "netlist_file": spec["netlist"]["file"],
        "output_gds": spec["output"]["gds_path"],
    }
    for name, pair in spec["gds_mapping"].items():
        ctx["layer." + name.lower() + ".gds"] = _numlist([pair[0], pair[1]])
        ctx["layer." + name.lower() + ".name"] = _q(name)
    return ctx


def has_placeholders(text):
    return PLACEHOLDER_RE.search(text) is not None


def render_template(text, ctx):
    def repl(m):
        for grp in ("k", "a", "l", "p", "d", "h"):
            key = m.group(grp)
            if key is not None:
                return str(ctx.get(key, m.group(0)))
        return m.group(0)
    return PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(repl, text)


def has_residue(text):
    return RESIDUE_RE.search(text) is not None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Report / manifest + main entry points
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def gen_report(spec):
    return {
        "process": spec["process"],
        "design_name": spec["design_name"],
        "file_count": len(EIGHT_FILES),
        "files": EIGHT_FILES,
        "sourcing_order": SOURCE_ORDER,
        "placement_mode": spec["placement"]["mode"],
        "netlist_mode": spec["netlist"]["mode"],
        "layer_count": len(spec["gds_mapping"]),
        "via_count": len(spec["via_definitions"]),
        "device_class_count": len(spec["placement"]["device_classes"]),
        "cell_count": len(spec["cell_list"]),
        "generator": "generate_autocell_flow.py",
    }


_GENERATORS = {
    "run.tcl": gen_run,
    "layers.tcl": gen_layers,
    "layer_functions.tcl": gen_layer_functions,
    "viadefs.tcl": gen_viadefs,
    "globals.tcl": gen_globals,
    "rules.tcl": gen_rules,
    "place.tcl": gen_place,
    "route.tcl": gen_route,
}


def generate_flow(spec_path, skeleton_dir, out_dir):
    """Read the spec + skeleton and write the eight TCL files + report.json.

    Returns the report dict.
    """
    spec = normalize_spec(load_json(spec_path))
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    ctx = build_context(spec)

    for name in EIGHT_FILES:
        skel_path = os.path.join(skeleton_dir, name) if skeleton_dir else None
        skel = read_text(skel_path)
        content = None
        if skel is not None and has_placeholders(skel):
            content = render_template(skel, ctx)
        if content is None or has_residue(content):
            # Fall back to fully spec-driven generation, guaranteeing a valid,
            # internally-consistent and placeholder-free flow.
            content = _GENERATORS[name](spec)
        write_text(os.path.join(out_dir, name), content)

    report = gen_report(spec)
    write_text(os.path.join(out_dir, "report.json"),
               json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    return report


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="AutoCell TCL flow generator")
    ap.add_argument("--spec", required=True, help="path to spec JSON")
    ap.add_argument("--skeleton", default=None, help="path to skeleton template dir")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output directory")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    report = generate_flow(args.spec, args.skeleton, args.out)
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# =============================================================================
# AutoCell DRAM Example - CAD Layers (1/7)
#
# Declares every physical layer that may appear in the layout together with its
# GDS stream (layer#, datatype). Layer *roles* (functions) are assigned in
# layer_functions.tcl.
#
# IC context (see doc/knowledge/design-rules-glossary.md):
#   A layout is the geometric blueprint of shapes on every mask layer. These
#   layers map onto a real foundry stack: AA (active area) holds the channel,
#   NW is the N-well for PMOS, GATE is the poly gate, NPLUS/PPLUS are the
#   N+/P+ source-drain implants, M0/M1 are the wiring (metal) layers and
#   VIA1/CT are the vertical plugs between layers.
# =============================================================================
tech add_layer -name "AA"         -gds {1 18}   ;# active area - silicon island / channel + S-D
tech add_layer -name "BORDER"     -gds {127 0}  ;# cell frame / scribe helper (non-device)
tech add_layer -name "GATE"       -gds {26 16}  ;# poly gate - control electrode over the channel
tech add_layer -name "GATE_DUMMY" -gds {26 262} ;# dummy poly - non-functional filler for density
tech add_layer -name "NPLUS"      -gds {17 71}  ;# N+ source-drain implant (NMOS)
tech add_layer -name "PPLUS"      -gds {16 71}  ;# P+ source-drain implant (PMOS)
tech add_layer -name "M0"         -gds {30 30}  ;# metal-1 - main wiring + power-rail layer
tech add_layer -name "M1"         -gds {46 0}   ;# metal-2 - upper wiring layer
tech add_layer -name "NRVT"       -gds {9 43}   ;# Vt-implant adjust marker (NMOS threshold)
tech add_layer -name "NW"         -gds {3 0}    ;# N-well - doped well hosting the PMOS devices
tech add_layer -name "CT"         -gds {26 31}  ;# contact - plug landing on active or poly
tech add_layer -name "PPLUS_SD"   -gds {11 0}   ;# P+ source-drain marker / guard structures
tech add_layer -name "VIA1"       -gds {50 0}   ;# via - vertical connection M0 <-> M1
tech add_layer -name "text1"      -gds {30 251} ;# text label - metal-1 pin names (e.g. VDD/VSS)
tech add_layer -name "text2"      -gds {30 252} ;# text label - metal-2 pin names
tech add_layer -name "text3"      -gds {30 253} ;# text label - poly pin names

===== dram/layer_functions.tcl =====
# =============================================================================
# AutoCell DRAM Example - Layer Functions (2/7)
#
# Assigns a *function* to each CAD layer. Functions drive device recognition,
# contact landing, well/implant polarity and pin/text marking during layout
# extraction, DRC and LVS. (Requires the layers from layers.tcl.)
#
# IC context (see doc/knowledge/design-rules-glossary.md):
#   A bare GDS layer number only identifies a mask. The *function* is the
#   semantic role - what that mask actually does on silicon. Recognising
#   "this shape is poly", "this is an N+ implant" or "this well is nwell"
#   is what lets AutoCell reconstruct transistors and run DRC/LVS.
# =============================================================================
tech set_layer_function -layer "AA"         -functions { "pdiff" "ndiff" }      ;# active = diffusion region
tech set_layer_function -layer "BORDER"     -functions { "border" "psub" }      ;# frame + p-substrate marker
tech set_layer_function -layer "GATE"       -functions { "poly" "pgate" "ngate" } ;# poly gate over P/N active
tech set_layer_function -layer "GATE_DUMMY" -functions { "poly_dummy" }          ;# filler poly (no device)
tech set_layer_function -layer "NPLUS"      -functions { "nplus" }               ;# N+ source-drain implant
tech set_layer_function -layer "PPLUS"      -functions { "pplus" }               ;# P+ source-drain implant
tech set_layer_function -layer "M0"         -functions { "m1" }                  ;# metal-1 wiring
tech set_layer_function -layer "M1"         -functions { "m2" }                  ;# metal-2 wiring
tech set_layer_function -layer "NW"         -functions { "nwell" }               ;# N-well (PMOS body)
tech set_layer_function -layer "CT"         -functions { "pcont" "ncont" "poly_cont" } ;# contacts to S/D & poly
tech set_layer_function -layer "VIA1"       -functions { "via1" }                ;# M0-M1 via
tech set_layer_function -layer "text1"      -functions { "m1_label" }            ;# M1 pin name text
tech set_layer_function -layer "text2"      -functions { "m2_label" }            ;# M2 pin name text
tech set_layer_function -layer "text3"      -functions { "poly_label" }          ;# poly pin name text

===== dram/viadefs.tcl =====
# =============================================================================
# AutoCell DRAM Example - Via Definitions (3/7)
#
# A via definition ("viadef") stacks two conductive layers through a cut layer,
# including the cut-array layout and the required enclosure on each layer.
# (Requires the layers from layers.tcl. The named via stacks are mapped for use
# in route.tcl.)
#
# IC context (see doc/knowledge/design-rules-glossary.md):
#   A via is the vertical plug connecting one metal/poly level to another.
#   The "enclosure" (layer*_enc) is how far the surrounding layer must overlap
#   the cut so the contact survives mask misalignment - the same idea as foundry
#   enclosure rules (e.g. M1.E.2, CS.E.1/2).
# =============================================================================
# Contact: AA (source/drain) up to M0 - the device-to-metal plug (like CS/CA in a DRM).
tech add_viadef -name "CT_AA" -cut_layer "CT" -layer1 "AA" -layer2 "M0" \
    -cut_rowcol {1 1} -cut_size {0.07 0.3} -cut_space {0.375 0.375} \
    -layer1_enc {0.115 0.115} -layer2_enc {0.115 0.115}
# Contact: poly GATE up to M0 - two orientations (landing on horizontal / vertical poly).
tech add_viadef -name "CT_GT_1" -cut_layer "CT" -layer1 "GATE" -layer2 "M0" \
    -cut_rowcol {1 1} -cut_size {0.07 0.3} -cut_space {0 0} \
    -layer1_enc {0.09 0.05} -layer2_enc {0.115 0.115}
tech add_viadef -name "CT_GT_2" -cut_layer "CT" -layer1 "GATE" -layer2 "M0" \
    -cut_rowcol {1 1} -cut_size {0.3 0.07} -cut_space {0 0} \
    -layer1_enc {0.05 0.09} -layer2_enc {0.115 0.115}
# Via: M0 up to M1 - the metal-to-metal vertical connection (VIA1 in a DRM).
tech add_viadef -name "Via1" -cut_layer "VIA1" -layer1 "M0" -layer2 "M1" \

# =============================================================================
# AutoCell DRAM Example - Global Nets (4/7)
#
# Tells AutoCell which net names are power / ground (supply) rails. These are
# used for the PG connectors, power-rail drawing and LVS so that arbitrary
# supply name variants are recognised as VDD/VSS.
#
# IC context (see doc/knowledge/IC_Design_Glossary_for_Beginners.md):
#   Every CMOS gate needs a supply: VDD (the high rail the PMOS "pull-up"
#   drives) and VSS / ground (the low rail the NMOS "pull-down" drives).
#   Listing all common spelling variants here lets a net named any of them be
#   treated as the same global supply during LVS and power-rail routing.
# =============================================================================
tech set_global_net -vdd { VDD VCC } -vss { VSS } \
    -vpw { vss! vss vpw! vpw vbn! vbn vbb! vbb gnd! gnd VSS! VSS VPW! VPW VBN! VBN VBB! VBB GND! GND } \
    -vnw { vpp! vpp vnw! vnw vdd! vdd vcc! vcc vbp! vbp VPP! VPP VNW! VNW VDD! VDD VCC! VCC VBP! VBP }
# -vpw / -vnw list the potential (body) supply variants for the P-well / N-well
# taps - i.e. the substrate biases tied to VSS and VDD respectively.
